en.Primitive value: A number or boolean stored as its own value, rather than an object reference.
en.Cast: An explicit request to convert a value; it may discard information.
en.Overflow: A mathematical result outside a type’s representable range.
en.Invariant: A fact true before and after each completed iteration.
en.Short-circuit: Skip the second Boolean operand when the first already decides the result.
en.Progress measure: A bounded quantity that moves toward termination.
en.Argument: The value supplied at a method call.
en.Parameter: A new variable initialized with a copy of an argument value.
en.Alias: Another reference reaching the same object.
en.Ragged array: An array of rows whose lengths need not match.
en.Shallow copy: A new outer container that still shares referenced inner objects.
en.Component type: The type an array accepts for its elements.
en.Stack frame: The part of the stack that holds the parameters and local variables of one method call.
en.Heap: The area where objects and arrays live until they can no longer be reached.
en.Reference: A value that identifies an object, drawn as an arrow; it may also be null.
en.Reachable: An object that some root can reach through a chain of references.
en.Mark-and-sweep: A collection method that marks everything reachable from the roots, then frees the rest.
en.Immutable: An object’s logical value cannot be changed after construction.
en.UTF-16 code unit: One 16-bit unit used by Java String indexing.
en.StringBuilder: A mutable buffer for assembling text before creating a String.
en.Constructor: Code that establishes a new instance’s initial state.
en.Defensive copy: A copy made to prevent outside aliases from changing protected state.
en.Token: One input unit separated according to a reader’s delimiter rules.
en.Line boundary: The end of a logical input line, handled differently from a numeric token.
en.Resource ownership: Responsibility for closing a resource after use.
en.Binary layout: The agreed order, widths, and representation of stored fields.
en.Byte order: The sequence in which high- and low-order bytes are written.
en.Truncated record: A record ending before all required field bytes arrive.
en.List: An ordered sequence that may contain equal elements more than once.
en.Set: A collection that keeps at most one member for each equality value.
en.Map: A relation from each key to one current associated value.
en.Identity: Whether two references denote the exact same object.
en.Value equality: A class-defined rule saying two objects represent the same logical value.
en.Hash collision: Unequal values share a hash code, which is legal.
en.Subtype: A type usable through a supertype while preserving its promised behavior.
en.Composition: An object holds a collaborator and delegates work to it.
en.Substitutability: Clients retain valid expectations when an implementation is replaced by a subtype.
en.Overload: Methods share a name but differ in parameter lists.
en.Override: A subtype supplies an implementation for an inherited instance method.
en.Receiver: The object on which an instance method is invoked.
en.Abstract method: A declared operation whose implementation must be supplied by a concrete subtype.
en.Interface: A named capability contract that different classes can implement.
en.Default method: An inherited instance-method implementation supplied by an interface.
en.Type parameter: A placeholder type declared by a generic class or method.
en.Bound: A requirement restricting which types may replace a type parameter.
en.Erasure: Compilation removes much generic type information while preserving inserted checks and casts.
en.Invariance: List<Integer> is not a subtype of List<Number>, despite the element relationship.
en.Producer: An argument from which the current method reads values.
en.Consumer: An argument into which the current method writes values.
en.Iterator: An object storing one traversal’s cursor and operations.
en.Reachability: Whether a chain of live references can still reach an object.
en.Root: An execution or static reference from which reachability begins.
en.Checked exception: An exception the compiler requires callers to catch or declare.
en.Unwinding: Leaving active method calls while searching for a matching handler.
en.Exceptional guarantee: What remains true about state when an operation fails.
en.Custom exception: An exception class you write to name a failure in your own program's terms.
en.Unchecked exception: A RuntimeException or Error that needs no catch or throws.
en.Cause: The earlier exception stored inside a new one, available through getCause().
en.Exception hierarchy: A tree of exception classes in which a subclass is a more specific failure.
en.serialVersionUID: A version number that exception classes declare because they are serializable.
en.Enum constant: One named instance from a fixed enum-defined set.
en.Transition: A rule taking a current state and event to a next state or rejection.
en.Stable code: An explicit external identifier independent of declaration position.
en.Fixture: The prepared objects and inputs for one test case.
en.Boundary case: An input on or near a rule’s acceptance limit.
en.Regression test: A retained test that detects a previously understood defect returning.
en.Base case: A case answered without another recursive call.
en.Memoization: Caching a result under the inputs that determine it.
en.Call depth: The number of simultaneously active nested calls.
en.Functional interface: An interface with one abstract method that supplies a lambda’s target type.
en.Capture: Using a value or reference from the surrounding scope in a lambda.
en.Effectively final: A local variable assigned once and never reassigned after initialization.
en.Reproducer: A small input and program that reliably reveal a failure.
en.Hypothesis: A specific explanation that predicts an observable result.
en.Precondition: A requirement that must hold when a method is called.
en.Package: A named group of classes that matches a folder and prevents name clashes.
en.Import: A statement that lets you use a short class name; it loads nothing.
en.Package-private: Access with no modifier: visible inside the same package only.
en.Protected: Visible in the same package and in subclasses, with the extra rule for other packages.
en.Generalisation: The UML relation for extends: a solid line with a hollow triangle at the parent.
en.Realisation: The UML relation for implements: a dashed line with a hollow triangle at the interface.
en.Multiplicity: A number or range, such as 1 or 0..*, showing how many objects take part in a link.
en.Javadoc: The tool and comment style that turn /** */ comments into HTML documentation.
en.Model: The data and rules that represent the application’s domain.
en.Event boundary: The place where an external action becomes a validated domain request.
en.Dependency injection: Passing a collaborator into an object instead of constructing a fixed one internally.

zh.基本类型值: 直接表示数值或布尔值，而非对象引用。
zh.强制类型转换: 显式请求转换数值，可能丢失信息。
zh.溢出: 数学结果超出类型可表示的范围。
zh.循环不变式: 每次完整迭代前后都成立的事实。
zh.短路求值: 第一个布尔操作数已决定结果时，不求第二个。
zh.进展度量: 朝终止方向变化、且有界的量。
zh.形参: 用实参值的副本初始化的新变量。
zh.别名: 指向同一对象的另一个引用。
zh.不规则数组: 各行长度不必相同的数组。
zh.浅复制: 新外层容器仍共享其引用的内部对象。
zh.元素类型: 数组允许存入的元素类型。
zh.栈帧: 栈中保存一次方法调用的参数和局部变量的部分。
zh.堆: 存放对象和数组的区域，它们一直存在到再也无法到达为止。
zh.引用: 标识某个对象的值，画成箭头；它也可以是 null。
zh.可达: 某个根能通过一串引用到达的对象。
zh.标记清除: 一种回收方法：先标记从根可达的所有对象，再释放其余对象。
zh.不可变: 对象构造后，其逻辑值不能改变。
zh.UTF-16 编码单元: Java 字符串索引使用的一个 16 位单元。
zh.可变字符串构建器: 创建 String 前用于组合文本的可变缓冲区。
zh.对象不变式: 每个可用对象状态都必须满足的规则。
zh.构造器: 建立新实例初始状态的代码。
zh.防御性复制: 为防止外部别名改变受保护状态而创建的副本。
zh.词法项: 按读取器分隔规则划分的一个输入单位。
zh.行边界: 逻辑输入行的结尾，其处理方式与数字词法项不同。
zh.资源所有权: 使用后负责关闭资源的责任。
zh.二进制布局: 存储字段约定的顺序、宽度与表示方式。
zh.字节序: 高位与低位字节写出的顺序。
zh.截断记录: 所需字段字节尚未完整到达就结束的记录。
zh.列表: 可重复包含相等元素的有序序列。
zh.集合: 每种相等值最多保留一个成员的容器。
zh.映射: 每个键对应一个当前关联值的结构。
zh.对象身份: 两个引用是否表示完全同一个对象。
zh.值相等: 类定义的规则，判断两个对象是否表示相同逻辑值。
zh.哈希冲突: 不相等值拥有相同哈希码，这是合法情况。
zh.子类型: 一种可以通过父类型来使用，同时保持父类型所承诺的行为的类型。
zh.组合: 一个对象持有一个协作者，并把工作委托给它去做。
zh.可替换性: 当一个实现被它的子类型替换时，客户端所抱有的合理期望仍然成立。
zh.重载: 方法同名，但参数列表不同。
zh.重写: 子类型为继承的实例方法提供实现。
zh.接收者: 实例方法被调用时作用的对象。
zh.抽象方法: 声明了操作，但实现需由具体子类型提供。
zh.接口: 不同类都可实现的命名能力契约。
zh.默认方法: 由接口提供、可继承的实例方法实现。
zh.类型参数: 由泛型类或方法声明的类型占位符。
zh.类型界限: 限制哪些类型能替换类型参数的要求。
zh.类型擦除: 编译移除许多泛型类型信息，同时保留所需检查与转换。
zh.不变性: 虽然元素类型有继承关系，List<Integer> 仍不是 List<Number> 子类型。
zh.生产者: 当前方法从中读取值的参数。
zh.消费者: 当前方法向其中写入值的参数。
zh.迭代器: 保存一次遍历游标与操作的对象。
zh.可达性: 是否仍有活跃引用链到达对象。
zh.根: 可达性搜索开始处的执行引用或静态引用。
zh.受检查异常: 编译器要求调用者捕获或声明的异常。
zh.调用栈展开: 寻找匹配处理器时退出活动方法调用的过程。
zh.异常保证: 操作失败时状态仍必须满足的保证。
zh.自定义异常: 你自己编写的异常类，用来按你程序的语言命名一种失败。
zh.非受检查异常: 不需要 catch 或 throws 的 RuntimeException 或 Error。
zh.原因: 保存在新异常里的先前异常，可通过 getCause() 取得。
zh.异常层次: 异常类组成的树，其中子类表示更具体的失败。
zh.serialVersionUID: 异常类因为可序列化而声明的版本号。
zh.枚举常量: 枚举定义的固定集合中的一个命名实例。
zh.状态转换: 把当前状态和事件变为下一状态或拒绝的规则。
zh.稳定编码: 不依赖声明位置的明确外部标识。
zh.测试初始环境: 单个测试案例准备的对象与输入。
zh.边界案例: 位于规则接受边界上或附近的输入。
zh.回归测试: 保留用于发现已理解缺陷再次出现的测试。
zh.基本情况: 无需继续递归即可回答的情况。
zh.记忆化: 按决定结果的输入缓存计算结果。
zh.调用深度: 同时活动的嵌套调用数量。
zh.函数式接口: 只有一个抽象方法、为 lambda 提供目标类型的接口。
zh.捕获: 在 lambda 内使用外围作用域的值或引用。
zh.事实上的 final: 初始化后不再重新赋值的局部变量。
zh.复现用例: 一个很小的输入和程序，能够可靠地让一个失败显现出来。
zh.假设: 一个具体的解释，它能够预测出一个可以被观察到的结果，所以可以拿来检验。
zh.前置条件: 在调用一个方法的时候，必须成立的一项要求。
zh.包: 一组有名字的类，与文件夹对应，并防止命名冲突。
zh.导入: 让你可以使用短类名的语句；它什么也不加载。
zh.包级私有: 不写修饰符的访问级别：只在同一个包内可见。
zh.protected: 在同一个包和子类中可见，对其他包有一条额外规则。
zh.泛化: UML 中表示 extends 的关系：实线，在父类一端有空心三角。
zh.实现: UML 中表示 implements 的关系：虚线，在接口一端有空心三角。
zh.多重性: 一个数或一个范围，如 1 或 0..*，表示一条关联中有多少个对象参与。
zh.Javadoc: 把 /** */ 注释变成 HTML 文档的工具和注释风格。
zh.模型: 表示应用领域数据与规则的部分。
zh.事件边界: 外部动作转换为经过验证的领域请求的位置。
zh.依赖注入: 把协作对象传入对象，而不是在内部固定创建它。
